summary: This is a markdown document that instructs an AI assistant how to capture a new task into a project's backlog. It defines a six-step procedure for creating a well-formed TODO file in the `.todos/` directory with a specific naming convention (four-digit ID plus slug), checking for duplicates, and filling in a standard template with priority, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

explanations.4: This line lists which tools the AI is allowed to use when executing this procedure — basic bash commands for listing and finding files, a custom script to generate the next ID number, and the ability to read and write files.
explanations.19: The 'slug' is a URL-friendly version of the task name: all lowercase, using only letters, numbers, and hyphens, without words like 'a' or 'the' at the start, and kept short so the filename stays readable.
explanations.31: Rather than manually counting existing IDs, always call this script because it searches through all TODO files (including ones in subfolders) and automatically returns the next sequential number padded to exactly 4 digits.
explanations.34: Legacy IDs that were recorded in the old 3-digit format (like '099') are left unchanged — we never rename them to the new 4-digit width, we only use 4 digits for new IDs going forward.
explanations.38: The filename itself is sacred and only contains the ID and slug; you must never put status like 'in-progress' or priority like 'urgent' in the filename because those belong in the file's metadata fields instead.
explanations.59: The 'header bullets' are the YAML-like fields (Priority, Batch, etc.) at the top of the template that other tools like `/todo-plan` will parse and understand — they must stay in that exact format.
